title: Choose the visual world for Scanferno
question: The roll assigned Station Bay. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Station Bay
options.lineage: Apparatus bay floors: sealed oxide concrete, stencilled bay numerals, safety striping
options.thesis: The briefing is marked out like an engine bay floor: stencilled numbers and painted lines tell you where to go.
options.viewport: Top band: who is trapped and where to enter, full width. Left: call transcript with facts pinned to the line that said them. Center: floor plan with huge stencilled A-D at its edges and search order as stencil numerals. Right: hazards and routes.
options.risk: Stencil type turns into costume if it spreads past numerals, side letters and section heads.

raised.raise: Safety yellow is reserved for what you act on or walk: entry door, exit route, primary buttons.
The next decision (trapped person, entry door) owns a full-width band above everything.
The floor plan owns the field; chrome recedes into the oxide ground with no card borders.
Every dispatch fact is pinned to the utterance that produced it, on one time axis.
Every number (meters, feet, confidence, clear time) is tabular and right-aligned.

options.label: Evacuation Plan
options.lineage: ISO 23601 'You are here' evacuation plans posted beside every door
options.thesis: The briefing reads like the evacuation plan on the wall, drawn for the crew going in instead of the people coming out.
options.viewport: Light laminated ground. Plan fills two-thirds with green egress arrows and red fire pictograms; a narrow legend column holds the call and briefing like the plan's key.
options.risk: Wayfinding signage is where most runs in this category land, and a light screen glares in a dark cab at night.

options.label: Carbon Coupon Book
options.lineage: Jet-age airline ticket wallets with carbon-copy coupons
options.thesis: Each dispatch update is a carbon coupon; a corrected fact is stamped VOID, never silently replaced.
options.viewport: Coupon stack on the left (one per record update, old values struck), plan in a ruled field box center, briefing as tabbed coupons right.
options.case: Fuses well on clarity: caller corrections become visible stamps. Loses on audience: officers don't identify with airline paper.
options.risk: Reads as travel nostalgia; dark-cab use forces a dark rendition of a paper world.

options.label: Warm Consumer App
options.viewport: Single column of cards with a bottom bar.
options.risk: Reads like a food-delivery app at a fire.
options.case: Loses both: officers don't identify with it, and one column hides the plan.
options.kept: Action color reserved strictly for things you can act on.

options.label: Vertical Feed
options.thesis: One briefing item owns the screen at a time.
options.viewport: One fact per screen, snap to the next.
options.risk: Loses the plan and the live call side by side.
options.case: Loses both: an officer needs plan, call and hazards at once.
options.kept: The next decision owns a full-width band.

options.label: Catalog Sleeve
options.thesis: Color codes stand in for words.
options.viewport: One plot owns a black field, labels decoded on hover.
options.case: Loses both: coded labels are the opposite of glanceable.
options.kept: One plot owns the field; chrome recedes.

options.label: Dance Score
options.thesis: The call as a vertical score read upward.
options.viewport: Dispatcher and caller columns flank a time staff.
options.risk: Notation officers would have to learn.
options.case: Loses both: unfamiliar notation, weak plan role.
options.kept: Facts sit on one strict time axis with their source line.

options.label: Datamatics
options.thesis: Pure black and white data density.
options.risk: No room for hazard red; strobing is unsafe.
options.case: Loses both: no state color, art over task.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A dark incident-ops dashboard (Grafana / PagerDuty class) executed cleanly.
canonCard.viewport: Top bar, three panels: call left, plan center, briefing right, at full craft.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other ops tool, including today's build.
